title: The Cambrian Explosion
sourceNote: Biên soạn dựa trên kiến thức cổ sinh vật học phổ thông (không sao chép nguyên văn Wikipedia).

sections.text: The Cambrian explosion refers to a relatively sudden appearance, roughly 538 million years ago, of a striking diversity of complex animal life in the fossil record, after more than three billion years during which life on Earth had consisted almost entirely of single-celled organisms and simple, soft-bodied multicellular forms. Within a geological interval lasting perhaps twenty to twenty-five million years, brief by the standards of Earth's four-and-a-half-billion-year history, representatives of most major animal groups alive today, including the ancestors of arthropods, molluscs, and early relatives of vertebrates, appear in the fossil record for the first time, many already bearing hard shells or exoskeletons that fossilise far more readily than soft tissue.

Much of what is known about Cambrian animals comes from a small number of exceptional fossil deposits, called Lagerstätten, where unusually favourable conditions preserved not only hard shells but also soft tissues that are normally lost entirely to decay. The most famous of these is the Burgess Shale, discovered in the Canadian Rocky Mountains in 1909 by the American palaeontologist Charles Doolittle Walcott, which preserves an extraordinarily detailed snapshot of Cambrian marine life, including many bizarre animals with no obvious modern equivalent. A comparable, slightly older deposit called the Chengjiang biota, discovered in China's Yunnan province in 1984, has since provided further detailed evidence of the same burst of early animal diversity.

Several explanations have been proposed for why this diversification happened when it did, and most researchers now regard the true answer as a combination of several contributing factors rather than any single decisive cause. A sharp rise in atmospheric and oceanic oxygen levels shortly before the Cambrian may have allowed animals to grow larger and support more energy-demanding tissues and behaviours than had previously been possible. The evolution of vision is thought by some researchers to have triggered an evolutionary arms race, since a predator that can see its prey creates powerful selective pressure favouring prey that can detect the predator in turn, or that develop hard defensive shells, which themselves further favour predators evolving harder mouthparts or better vision, a feedback loop that could accelerate diversification rapidly once it began.

The apparent suddenness of the Cambrian explosion troubled Charles Darwin himself, who acknowledged in On the Origin of Species that the abrupt appearance of complex animals, without an obvious long fossil record of simpler ancestral forms leading up to them, appeared at first glance to sit uneasily with his theory of gradual evolutionary change by natural selection. Darwin argued that the fossil record of the time was simply too incomplete to have preserved the earlier, presumably soft-bodied ancestors, and subsequent discoveries have partly vindicated this view: fossils of soft-bodied, complex, though comparatively simple, multicellular animals dating from the preceding Ediacaran period, roughly 635 to 538 million years ago, have since been found at numerous sites worldwide, suggesting that animal evolution was already well underway before the Cambrian explosion made it dramatically visible in the fossil record.

Rather than representing the literal sudden invention of complex animal life from nothing, most palaeontologists today interpret the Cambrian explosion as principally a dramatic increase in the rate at which animals evolved hard, readily fossilised body parts, combined with a genuine and rapid diversification of body plans that was likely already building on genetic innovations, particularly in the genes controlling embryonic development, that had arisen somewhat earlier during the preceding Ediacaran period. Under this view, the Cambrian explosion is less a mysterious violation of gradual evolution than an unusually well-preserved and dramatic record of a period of genuinely rapid, but not instantaneous, evolutionary change.

questions.instruction:
The passage has 5 sections, A-E.
Choose the correct heading for each section from the list of headings below.
Write the correct number, i-vii, as your answer.
NB There are more headings than sections, so you will not use them all.

List of Headings
i	What happened, and how quickly it happened
ii	Fossil sites that preserved soft tissue in exceptional detail
iii	Several factors that may have driven the diversification
iv	How it appeared to challenge Darwin's own theory
v	A more gradual picture that later evidence supported
vi	Dating the rocks using radioactive decay
vii	Why most Cambrian animals eventually went extinct
questions.explanation: Đoạn A mô tả sự kiện bùng nổ Cambri là gì và diễn ra nhanh tới mức nào (20-25 triệu năm). Đúng tiêu đề i.
Đoạn B nói về các mỏ hoá thạch đặc biệt (Lagerstätten) như Burgess Shale và Chengjiang lưu giữ cả mô mềm. Đúng tiêu đề ii.
Đoạn C nêu vài giả thuyết: tăng oxy, tiến hoá thị giác gây chạy đua vũ trang tiến hoá. Đúng tiêu đề iii.
Đoạn D nói sự bùng nổ đột ngột này từng khiến chính Darwin lo ngại nó mâu thuẫn với thuyết tiến hoá dần dần của ông. Đúng tiêu đề iv.
Đoạn E nói các nhà cổ sinh vật học nay coi đây là quá trình tiến hoá nhanh nhưng không tức thời, dựa trên nền tảng đã có từ kỷ Ediacara. Đúng tiêu đề v.

Write
TRUE  if the statement agrees with the information

questions.prompt: Before the Cambrian explosion, life on Earth had existed for more than three billion years.
questions.explanation: Đoạn A: 'after more than three billion years during which life on Earth had consisted almost entirely of single-celled organisms'. Đúng ý đề nên TRUE.

questions.prompt: The Chengjiang biota was discovered before the Burgess Shale.
questions.explanation: Đoạn B: Burgess Shale phát hiện năm 1909, Chengjiang phát hiện năm 1984 — Chengjiang sau, không phải trước. FALSE.

questions.prompt: Most researchers now believe a single decisive cause fully explains the Cambrian explosion.
questions.explanation: Đoạn C: 'most researchers now regard the true answer as a combination of several contributing factors rather than any single decisive cause'. Nhiều yếu tố kết hợp, không phải một nguyên nhân duy nhất. FALSE.

questions.prompt: Darwin believed the incompleteness of the fossil record explained the apparently sudden appearance of complex animals.
questions.explanation: Đoạn D: 'Darwin argued that the fossil record of the time was simply too incomplete to have preserved the earlier... ancestors'. Đúng ý đề nên TRUE.

questions.prompt: Fossils from the Ediacaran period have been found only at a single site worldwide.
questions.explanation: Đoạn D: hoá thạch Ediacara 'have since been found at numerous sites worldwide'. Nhiều nơi, không phải một nơi duy nhất. FALSE.

questions.instruction:
Complete the sentences below.
Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.
questions.prompt: Exceptional fossil deposits that preserve soft tissue are called ________.
questions.explanation: Đoạn B: 'a small number of exceptional fossil deposits, called Lagerstätten'. Đáp án Lagerstätten.

questions.prompt: The Burgess Shale was discovered in 1909 by ________.
questions.explanation: Đoạn B: 'discovered in the Canadian Rocky Mountains in 1909 by the American palaeontologist Charles Doolittle Walcott'. Đáp án Charles Doolittle Walcott.

questions.prompt: A rise in evolutionary pressure between predator and prey senses is described as an evolutionary ________ race.
questions.explanation: Đoạn C: 'may have... triggered an evolutionary arms race'. Đáp án arms.

questions.prompt: Darwin discussed this problem in his book On the Origin of ________.
questions.explanation: Đoạn D: 'who acknowledged in On the Origin of Species'. Đáp án Species.

questions.prompt: The period immediately before the Cambrian, roughly 635 to 538 million years ago, is called the ________ period.
questions.explanation: Đoạn D: 'the preceding Ediacaran period, roughly 635 to 538 million years ago'. Đáp án Ediacaran.
